mainTopic: Whether the order of lists in a משנה matters (רב הונא's rule and its exceptions), and the ranking of סקילה versus שריפה
overview: The new משנה lists the four death penalties of בית דין: סקילה, שריפה, הרג, and חנק. רבי שמעון gives them in a different order. The גמרא opens with רב הונא's rule that the order of a list in a משנה usually does not matter, except for the seven substances used to test a stain. Other אמוראים suggest more lists whose order matters: the ארבע מיתות, the יום הכפורים service, and the תמיד. The גמרא explains why רב הונא did not count each one. רב הונא's rule also teaches that the order of חליצה is only the ideal way, as רב יהודה and a ברייתא show. In the same way, the order of the כהן's garments in a משנה is not the order of dressing, since the trousers go on first. Finally, the גמרא starts to explain the משנה's ranking: סקילה seems more severe than שריפה. Then it argues the opposite, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The four death penalties given to the court
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the four kinds of execution that בית דין may carry out: סקילה, שריפה, הרג, and חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Four kinds of death penalty were given to בית דין: stoning, burning, killing by the sword, and strangulation.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens by listing the four death penalties that בית דין can carry out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the base list for the whole discussion. Its order (סקילה first, חנק last) is usually understood as going from the most severe to the least severe. The גמרא will soon ask whether the order of a list like this means anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Were given over to the court to carry out

phrases.english: MISHNA: Four types of death penalty
were given over to the court:
stoning, burning, killing, and strangulation.
phrases.notes: "Killing" (הרג) here means execution by the sword.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new משנה and the new chapter's topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין has four death penalties: סקילה, שריפה, הרג, חנק.

steps.title: רבי שמעון lists the death penalties in a different order
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון gives the same four penalties in a different order: שריפה, סקילה, חנק, הרג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: burning, stoning, strangulation, and killing by the sword.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the order of the list in the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions name the same four penalties. The only difference is the order. רבי שמעון puts שריפה before סקילה and חנק before הרג. This disagreement suggests that the order of this list carries meaning, probably which penalty is more severe.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה
And killing by the sword (last on רבי שמעון's list)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not adding or removing any penalty. He agrees on all four and only argues about the order.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
burning, stoning, strangulation, and killing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different order for the same list from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון the order is שריפה, סקילה, חנק, הרג.

steps.title: This was the procedure for those who are stoned
steps.stepSummary: A closing line says that the process described before was the procedure for executing someone by סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the procedure for those who are stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: A short line labels what came before: the execution steps described earlier were the procedure for סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line looks back at the previous chapter, which described the stoning process. It tells the learner that the earlier details belong specifically to סקילה. It does not add a new law.

phrases.english: This is the procedure of those who are stoned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A separate labeling line that refers back to the stoning procedure described before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earlier description was the procedure for סקילה.

steps.title: רב הונא: the order of a list usually does not matter
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches that when חכמים give a list, the order means nothing, except for the seven stain-testing substances.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא said in the name of רב סחורא, who said in the name of רב הונא: Wherever the חכמים taught by way of a list, there is no 'first and last.' The only exception is the seven substances.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a general rule about lists in משניות: their order normally has no significance, with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule matters right away, because our משנה is a list and רבי שמעון argues about its order. רב הונא says that, in general, you should not read meaning into the order of a list. He names one exception, the seven substances, which the גמרא is about to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
By way of a list or count
There is no 'earlier and later'; the order does not matter
Seven substances (used to test a stain)

steps.confusionAlert: Our own משנה seems to care about order, since רבי שמעון argues about it. Keep this tension in mind. Steps 7–9 deal with exactly this question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for reading any list in a משנה. It warns you not to assume that 'first' means 'most important' unless there is a reason.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: that Rav Sechora said that Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנוּ חֲכָמִים דֶּרֶךְ מִנְיָין,
phrases.english: Wherever the Sages taught by way of a list,
there is no earlier and later,
phrases.notes: In other words, the order of the items in the list doesn't matter.

phrases.english: except for the seven substances.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנוּ חֲכָמִים דֶּרֶךְ מִנְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a general rule about lists, relevant to the list in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of a list in a משנה has no significance, except for the seven substances.

steps.title: The משנה of the seven stain-testing substances
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that lists the seven substances applied to a stain.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Seven substances are applied to a stain: bland saliva, water of crushed beans, urine, natron, lye, Kimolian earth, and potash.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for רב הונא's exception. This step sets up the proof, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, this list does not show that order matters. It only names the seven substances. The proof comes from the ending of that same משנה, which the גמרא quotes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A stain (here, one that may be blood)
They apply or pass over (rub the substance on)
Bland saliva, from someone who has not eaten yet that day

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
seven substances are applied to the stain:
bland spittle, and moisture of grits,
phrases.notes: "Bland spittle" is the saliva of someone who hasn't tasted anything yet that morning.

phrases.english: and urine, and natron,
and lye, Kimolian earth, and potash.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the source of the exception named in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's exception that the order of the seven substances matters
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת נדה listing the seven substances

steps.title: The ending of that משנה proves the order matters
steps.stepSummary: The ending of the משנה says that applying the substances out of order, or all at once, accomplishes nothing. This proves that their order is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the end of that משנה teaches: If he applied them not in their order, or applied all seven at once, he has done nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual proof: the end of that משנה says that using the substances out of order does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since doing it out of order makes the whole test worthless, the order of this list must be required. That is why the seven substances are the one exception to רב הונא's rule. It also shows what a list looks like when its order really matters: the text says so outright.

keyTerms.meaning: And it teaches in the last part (of that משנה)
He did nothing at all; it does not count

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's rule: the order of a list in a משנה usually does not matter. The exception is the seven stain-testing substances, where the משנה itself says that doing them out of order accomplishes nothing.

phrases.english: And it is taught in the latter clause:
if he applied them not in their order,
or applied all seven of them at once,
he has done nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 5 by quoting the end of the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the order of the seven substances is required
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the משנה in מסכת נדה: out of order, he has done nothing

steps.title: The four death penalties are also in exact order
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא סבא, quoting רב, adds the ארבע מיתות to the lists whose order matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא the elder said in the name of רב: the list of the four death penalties is also given in an order that matters.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds a second exception to רב הונא's rule. He says the order of the ארבע מיתות is also meant exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said only the stain list has a meaningful order. רב פפא סבא says the list of סקילה, שריפה, הרג, חנק is also ranked on purpose. The word אף ("also") shows he is adding to רב הונא's exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Also. Here it adds one more item to the list of exceptions.
The four death penalties of בית דין.
In the name of. He is quoting someone else.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa the elder said in the name of Rav:
Also the four death penalties.
phrases.notes: He means: add this to רב הונא's exception from step 4. This list's order counts too.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר: אַף אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second exception to רב הונא's rule after the stain list was proven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of the ארבע מיתות is exact and meaningful.

steps.title: Proof: רבי שמעון argues about the order
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי שמעון disputes the order, the order must be meant exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי שמעון argues about it, we learn that the order is taught exactly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for רב פפא סבא's claim. רבי שמעון bothers to argue about the order, so the order must matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the order meant nothing, nobody would argue about it. רבי שמעון gave a different order (step 2), so both sides must think the order shows which death is more severe.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. A conclusion formula.

phrases.english: Since Rabbi Shimon disagrees,
learn from this that it is taught exactly.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָא מִפְּלִיג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דַּוְקָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 7's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the order of the ארבע מיתות is exact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's disagreement about the order (step 2).

steps.title: Why רב הונא left it out: it is a disputed list
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא only counted lists that no one argues about.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רב הונא, was not talking about a case where there is a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא did not list the ארבע מיתות. He only meant lists with no disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא agrees the order of the ארבע מיתות matters. He left it off because the correct order there is disputed. His rule only covers lists where everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other opinion
He is not talking about it

phrases.english: And the other one is not speaking about a dispute.
phrases.notes: "The other one" is רב הונא from step 4, who listed only the stain substances.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב הונא's shorter list against step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רב הונא's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא left out the ארבע מיתות because he thought their order means nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: He left them out only because their order is disputed. His rule covers only undisputed lists.

steps.title: The Yom Kippur service is also in exact order
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds the order of the יום הכפורים service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the order of the יום הכפורים service is also exact.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds a third list whose order matters: the כהן גדול's service on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the word אף adds to רב הונא's exceptions. This time the claim is about the steps of the עבודה, not a list of rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of "the Day", meaning the יום הכפורים service

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Also the order of the Day,
phrases.notes: "The Day" means יום הכפורים, the order of the כהן גדול's service.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אַף סֵדֶר יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another candidate exception, parallel to step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of the יום הכפורים service is essential.

steps.title: Proof: a משנה says out-of-order work is worthless
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that doing a יום הכפורים step too early accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: all the יום הכפורים actions said in order — if he did one before another, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a משנה as proof. It says that changing the order of the יום הכפורים service makes it count for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the stain proof in step 6. The order is required so strictly that breaking it cancels the act.

keyTerms.meaning: Did something earlier, put it first
He did nothing at all; the act does not count

phrases.english: As we learned: all the actions of Yom Kippur
that are stated in order,
if he did one action before another,
phrases.notes: "He" is the כהן גדול doing the service.

phrases.english: he has not done anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂה יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הָאֲמוּרִים עַל הַסֵּדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That the order of the יום הכפורים service is essential.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה ruling that doing a step out of order accomplishes nothing.

steps.title: Why רב הונא left it out: it is only a stringency
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא saw the יום הכפורים rule as just a חומרא, not a ranking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one: that is merely a stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא did not count the יום הכפורים order. He saw it as a special strict rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יום הכפורים order is required, but not because the list ranks anything. It is an extra strictness for that service. So it does not show that a list's order carries meaning.

phrases.english: And the other one: that is merely a stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב הונא against step 10–11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יום הכפורים order should count as an exception to רב הונא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is only a חומרא of that service, so it is not the kind of meaningful list רב הונא meant.

steps.title: The daily offering is also in exact order
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע adds the סדר תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: the order of the תמיד is also exact.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא adds one more candidate: the order of the daily תמיד offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier additions, this uses אף to extend רב הונא's exception. This רב הונא is a different person from the רב הונא in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the daily offering in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is a different אמורא from the רב הונא who made the original rule in step 4.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Also the order of the daily offering,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: אַף סֵדֶר תָּמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third candidate exception, parallel to steps 7 and 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of the תמיד service is exact.

steps.title: Proof: the משנה calls it "the order"
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with "this is the order of the תמיד", showing the order is intended.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה says about it: "This is the order of the תמיד."
steps.whatsHappening: The proof is the closing line of the משנה about the תמיד, which calls it "the order".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it "the order" suggests the steps must follow that sequence. It is like the closing line about סקילה in step 3.

phrases.english: since it teaches about it
"This is the order of the daily offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the order of the תמיד is exact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's closing words "זהו סדר תמיד".

steps.title: Why רב הונא left it out: it is only the ideal way
steps.stepSummary: The תמיד order is only a מצוה, the best way to do it, not a requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one: that is merely for the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא did not count the תמיד. Its order is only the preferred way to do the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing the תמיד in order is ideal, but changing the order does not cancel the offering. So the order is not truly essential, and רב הונא's list stays as it was.

keyTerms.meaning: For the מצוה, as the best way, but not required

steps.whatToRemember: Three more lists were suggested as exceptions: the ארבע מיתות, the יום הכפורים service, and the תמיד. Each was explained for רב הונא: he did not speak about disputed lists, the יום הכפורים rule is a חומרא, and the תמיד order is only a מצוה. So his rule stands as he stated it.

phrases.english: And the other one: that is merely for the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב הונא against steps 13–14 and closes the series of additions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrading the requirement to a מצוה לכתחילה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "This is the order" means the תמיד's order is essential.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order is only the ideal way. Changing it does not cancel the offering, so רב הונא did not count it.

steps.title: The order of the חליצה ceremony is also not essential
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב הונא's rule (step 4) is meant to exclude חליצה: even though its משנה lists the steps in order, that order is not a strict requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this also excludes the מצוה of חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רב הונא's rule from step 4. It names a case the rule is meant to cover: חליצה, where doing the steps out of order does not ruin the ceremony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said that only the seven substances have an essential order. The word לאפוקי shows what that rule comes to exclude: the חליצה ceremony is taken out of the group of 'order is required' cases. The גמרא will prove this from רב יהודה and a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to take out of a group
The ceremony where the woman removes the brother-in-law's shoe, freeing her from יבום
The brother of a man who died without children / the widow

phrases.english: And to exclude the mitzva of חליצה,
phrases.notes: This is what רב הונא's rule from step 4 comes to exclude: the order of the חליצה steps is not a strict requirement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proposed additions to רב הונא's exceptions are deflected (steps 7–15), the גמרא names a case that רב הונא's rule comes to exclude.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of the חליצה ceremony is not essential. Doing it out of order still works.

steps.title: The משנה describing the start of חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the first steps: coming to בית דין, getting advice, then she speaks and he speaks, all in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: The מצוה of חליצה works like this. He and his יבמה come before בית דין. The judges give him advice that fits him, as the פסוק says, 'The elders of his city shall call him and speak to him.' She says, 'My brother-in-law refused…', and he says, 'I do not wish to take her.' They would say these in לשון הקודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה that shows the steps of חליצה in their order. This step covers the opening steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly lays out a set order: court, advice, her statement, then his statement. According to רב הונא's rule, this order is not a strict requirement. The גמרא brings the משנה so we can see what 'the order of חליצה' means.

keyTerms.meaning: Advice that fits him, for example whether to do יבום or חליצה

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
The mitzva of חליצה:

phrases.aramaic: בָּא הוּא וִיבִמְתּוֹ לִפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: He and his יבמה come before the court,

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ נוֹתְנִין לוֹ עֵצָה הַהוֹגֶנֶת לוֹ,
phrases.english: and they would give him advice that fits him,
as it is said:
"And the elders of his city shall call him and speak to him."
And she says: "My brother-in-law refused, etc."
And he says: "I do not wish to take her."
And they would say these in the holy language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה that shows the order of חליצה mentioned in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: What the order of the חליצה ceremony is

steps.title: The משנה continues: shoe, spitting, and the final words
steps.stepSummary: The משנה goes on: she removes his shoe, spits so the judges can see, and says the closing words from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His יבמה shall approach him before the elders, remove his shoe, and spit before him.' This means spit that the judges can see. 'And she shall answer and say: So shall be done to the man… and his name shall be called in Israel…'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing the steps. After the speaking come the actions: removing the shoe and spitting, and then her final statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the full order is clear: speaking first, then the shoe, then spitting, then her last words. The משנה also explains that the spit must be visible to the judges. This full order is what the גמרא will discuss next.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., the rest of the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: "בפניו" ("before him") is explained here as spit that the judges can see. The text doesn't say exactly where it lands.

phrases.english: "And his יבמה shall approach him before the eyes of the elders
and remove his shoe and spit before him":
spit that can be seen by the judges.
"And she shall answer and say: So shall be done to the man, etc.
and his name shall be called in Israel, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with the remaining steps of חליצה.
steps.raayaObject: The rest of the order of חליצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in יבמות 106b, quoting דברים 25:9-10

steps.title: רב יהודה sums up the order of חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה gives a short formula for the order: she reads, he reads, she removes the shoe, she spits, and she reads.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: The מצוה of חליצה is: she reads and he reads, she removes the shoe and spits, and she reads.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה puts the whole ceremony into one short list of steps. This sets up the next move, which asks whether this order is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His formula matches the משנה exactly: two statements first, then two actions, then her last statement. Since he only repeats what the משנה already says, the next step asks what he is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: She reads, and he reads (their פסוקים)

steps.whatToRemember: The order of חליצה is: she reads, he reads, she removes the shoe, she spits, she reads. The question is whether this order is a strict requirement or just the best way to do it.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
The mitzva of חליצה:
she reads and he reads,
phrases.notes: She says "My brother-in-law refused," and then he says "I do not wish to take her."

phrases.english: she removes the shoe and spits, and she reads.
phrases.notes: Her last reading is "So shall be done to the man."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the order from the משנה in a short formula, setting up the question in step 20 of what רב יהודה adds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of חליצה: she reads, he reads, she removes the shoe, she spits, she reads.
steps.whyThisMatters: Like the תמיד case in steps 14-15, a clearly stated order may look like a strict requirement. That sets up the same kind of question about חליצה.

steps.title: What did רב יהודה add? It is already in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה needed to state the order of חליצה, since the משנה already lays it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What is רב יהודה teaching us? It is already in the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's short formula from step 19. The full order of חליצה was already written in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17-18 showed the משנה describing every stage of חליצה in order. If רב יהודה only repeats that order, his statement seems to add nothing new. The גמרא needs to find his חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it, raised a question about it
What is he teaching us? (what is new here?)
It is already in the משנה

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What is he teaching us?
It is already in the Mishnah!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? מַתְנִיתִין הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's formula from step 19 as repeating the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's formula for the order of חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement that only repeats the משנה has no purpose.

steps.title: The order is the best way, but switching it is fine
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that his order is the מצוה, but if it is switched, the חליצה still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: the מצוה is to do it in this order, but if someone switched it, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה's new point is that the order is only the ideal way, not a requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells us the order, but it does not say whether changing it ruins the חליצה. רב יהודה adds that the order is a מצוה only, and a switched order still works. This fits רב הונא's rule from step 4, as applied to חליצה in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: The ideal way to do it is like this
We have no problem with it; it is still valid

steps.whatToRemember: The order of חליצה is the best way to do it, but doing it out of order is still valid.

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us:
The מצוה is to do it like this,
but if one switched it, we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by showing רב יהודה's new point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new detail not stated in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה only repeats the משנה's order.
steps.terutzMaskana: He teaches that the order is ideal but not required.

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees: switching the shoe and the spitting still works
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that whether the shoe was removed first or the spitting came first, the חליצה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: whether the removal of the shoe came before the spitting, or the spitting before the removal, what was done is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא directly states that the order of removing the shoe and spitting can be reversed. This backs up the idea that the order is only a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a ברייתא supports it)
What was done is done; it is valid

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Whether one put the removal of the shoe before the spitting,
or the spitting before the removal of the shoe —
what was done is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 21 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The order of חליצה is not required
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that reversing shoe removal and spitting is valid

steps.title: Excluding the משנה about the כהן's garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב הונא's rule also excludes the משנה listing the כהן's garments: its listed order is not the order in which they are put on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this excludes what we learned in a משנה: the כהן גדול serves in eight garments and an ordinary כהן in four: a tunic, trousers, a turban, and a belt. The כהן גדול adds a breastplate, an apron, a robe, and a headplate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that lists the כהן's garments and says it is excluded. This sets up the next step, which shows why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second example of רב הונא's rule. The garments משנה lists the tunic first, but that does not mean the tunic is put on first. The next step proves the trousers go on first, so the order of this list carries no meaning.

phrases.english: And this excludes what we learned in a Mishnah:
The High Priest serves in eight garments,
and the ordinary priest in four.
In a tunic, in trousers,
in a turban, and a belt.
The High Priest adds to them:
a breastplate, an apron, a robe, and a headplate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second example, after חליצה, of a list that רב הונא's rule excludes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רב הונא's rule, the garments משנה's listed order carries no meaning for the order of dressing.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the trousers go on first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that nothing is put on before the trousers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught: From where do we know that nothing comes before the trousers? As it says: 'and linen trousers shall be on his flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the garments משנה is not listing the dressing order, because the trousers must go on first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the trousers are 'on his flesh,' meaning right against the body, so they are first. Yet the משנה listed the tunic first. So the משנה's list is not the dressing order.

keyTerms.meaning: On his flesh, directly on the body

phrases.english: And it is taught: From where do we know
that nothing comes before the trousers?
As it is said:
"and linen trousers shall be on his flesh."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא דָּבָר קוֹדֵם לַמִּכְנָסַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves why step 23's משנה is excluded.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's listed order of garments is not the dressing order

steps.title: Then why does the תנא list the tunic first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה put the tunic first if the trousers are put on first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא, what is the reason he put the tunic first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a natural follow-up question about the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trousers go on first, the תנא of the משנה must have had some other reason to start with the tunic. The גמרא wants to know it.

phrases.english: And the tanna, what is the reason
he put the tunic first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה's wording in light of step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה lists the tunic first

steps.title: Because the פסוק lists it first
steps.stepSummary: The תנא followed the פסוק, which mentions the tunic first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק put it first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה simply follows the order of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק mentions the tunic before the trousers. The משנה copied the פסוק's listing order, not the dressing order.

phrases.english: Because the verse put it first.
phrases.notes: The same פסוק, ויקרא 16:4, mentions the tunic before the trousers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows the פסוק's listing order

steps.title: Why does the פסוק list the tunic first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק itself mentions the tunic first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק, what is the reason it put it first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes one level deeper and asks about the פסוק's own order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trousers are put on first, there must be a reason the תורה lists the tunic before them.

phrases.english: And the verse, what is the reason it put it first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on step 26's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק mentions the tunic before the trousers

steps.title: The tunic covers the whole body, so it is mentioned first
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק mentions the tunic first because it covers the entire body, making it more important.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it covers his whole body, it is preferred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the tunic is listed first because of its importance, not because it is put on first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tunic covers the whole body, so the תורה gives it first place in the list. This confirms that the listing order is about importance, while the dressing order starts with the trousers.
steps.whatToRemember: The garments list puts the tunic first because it is most important, but the trousers are actually put on first. So that list is not an order to follow. Like חליצה, it is a list that רב הונא's rule excludes.

phrases.english: Because it covers his entire body,
it is preferred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 and closes the garments discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tunic is listed first because it covers the whole body

steps.title: Stoning is more severe than burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list and states that סקילה is more severe than שריפה, because סקילה is the punishment for the מגדף and for one who worships עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה lists stoning, burning, and so on. Stoning is more severe than burning, because stoning is given to one who blasphemes and to one who worships idols.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה's order of death penalties. It gives a reason why סקילה comes before שריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the death penalties from most severe to least severe. To justify putting סקילה above שריפה, the גמרא looks at which sins get סקילה. The worst sins, the מגדף and עבודה זרה, are punished with סקילה, so סקילה must be the harsher death.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof here is not about how painful each death is. It works by looking at which sins get that punishment: the worse the sins, the more severe the punishment.

phrases.english: Stoning, burning, etc.
Stoning is more severe than burning,
since it is given to one who blasphemes
and to one who worships idols.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the סוגיא about the ranking of the death penalties.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סקילה is more severe than שריפה because it is given for the sins of the מגדף and עבודה זרה.

steps.title: What makes those sins so severe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the sins of the מגדף and עבודה זרה especially severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the severity of these sins?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the claim it just made. Why are blasphemy and idol worship the worst sins?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in the last step only works if these sins really are worse than others. So the גמרא asks what makes them so serious.

phrases.english: What is the severity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the proof given in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the sins of the מגדף and עבודה זרה count as the most severe.

steps.title: They attack the foundation of faith
steps.stepSummary: These sinners attack the very foundation of faith, God Himself, so their sins are the most severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he stretches out his hand against the foundation of faith.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מגדף and the idol worshipper go after the very root of faith.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most sins break one specific rule. Blasphemy and idol worship strike at God Himself, the base of everything. That makes them the worst sins, and so their punishment, סקילה, is the most severe.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'stretches out his hand', meaning he attacks
The foundation, the root principle of faith

phrases.english: Since he stretches out his hand against the fundamental principle.
phrases.notes: The 'fundamental principle' here means the very base of faith: God Himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: These sins attack the foundation of faith, so they are the most severe.

steps.title: On the contrary, burning is more severe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with אדרבה. Maybe שריפה is more severe, since it is given to a בת כהן who committed adultery.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, burning is more severe, because it is given to a כהן's daughter who committed adultery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ranking by using the same kind of proof the other way. Look at who gets שריפה: a בת כהן who sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 proved that סקילה is more severe from the sinners who get it. Now the גמרא uses that same method to argue the opposite: שריפה is given to a בת כהן who sinned, which might be an even worse sin. This puts the משנה's order in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, the opposite is true

phrases.english: On the contrary: burning is more severe,
since it is given to a priest's daughter who committed adultery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the method of step 29 around to argue for the opposite ranking.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 29 that סקילה is more severe than שריפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using the same method of judging a punishment by the sinners who get it, שריפה is given to a בת כהן who sinned, so maybe שריפה is the more severe one.

steps.title: What makes her sin so severe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the sin of the בת כהן especially severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the severity of her sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why her sin should count as worse than other sins. This mirrors the question it asked about סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if her sin really is especially serious. So the גמרא asks for that reason, just as it did in step 30.

phrases.english: And what is the severity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the challenge in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the sin of a בת כהן is especially severe.

steps.title: She shames her father too
steps.stepSummary: Her sin is severe because she shames not only herself but also her father, the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because she profanes her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the בת כהן's sin also shames her father, the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her sin harms more than just herself, because it brings shame on her father's holy status. This gives real strength to the claim that שריפה might be more severe. The challenge to the משנה's order now stands with a solid reason behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Profanes, shames, lowers the holiness of

steps.whatToRemember: There are now two sides. סקילה looks more severe because it punishes those who attack the foundation of faith. שריפה looks more severe because it punishes a בת כהן who also shames her father.

phrases.english: Since she profanes her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33, completing the challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her sin also shames her father, so it is especially severe.
